unroll/graph: Unroll the loop, and an RNN is just a deep graph: one copy of the step for every token, all sharing the same weights.
unroll/back: Backprop runs through it as through any graph, from the loss back to the first step. That is backprop through time.
unroll/factor: Each step back multiplies the gradient by that step's local derivative: W h h, times the slope of the tanh.
unroll/sum: And since W h h is used at every step, its gradient adds up one contribution from each of them.
products/scalar: Picture a single hidden unit, where each step back multiplies the gradient by the same number, a. Ten steps back, it has been multiplied by a to the tenth.
products/vanish: If a is one half, that is about one thousandth. The gradient vanishes: the early steps get almost none of it.
products/explode: If a is two, it is over a thousand. The gradient explodes, and the numbers soon grow too large to use.
clip/clip: Exploding gradients have a blunt fix: clip them. Pick a threshold, c, say one.
clip/check: Whenever the gradient's norm is over c, shrink the whole vector to length c. Here g is three, four, with norm five.
clip/scale: Multiply it by c over the norm, one fifth: zero point six and zero point eight. Same direction, shorter length.
clip/limit: Clipping only ever shrinks: it tames a gradient that explodes, but it cannot bring back one that has vanished.
